summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update8.json → valid=true). Adversarial re-scoping of the first A2 finding, plus a durable correction. Reading all five consensus handlers in admission order shows the earlier implication was an overreach: processRPC's only common check is the protocol-version header (raft.go:1390-1412), and while requestVote and requestPreVote really do reject an ineligible sender — and do so *before* the branch that adopts a higher term and becomes Follower (raft.go:1636-1672) — appendEntries (1440-1474) and installSnapshot (1842-1852) have no membership check at all and will adopt a higher term, record the sender as leader, and in installSnapshot's case install the configuration carried in the request. So the missing guard is not peculiar to TimeoutNow. Recorded as a correction attached to the existing knowledge id b692e1e41ba940c78dc240498acfbdc1-knowledge-2 (changed_premise explains that the plural phrasing invited reading a local guard as an RPC-surface property, narrows the earlier interpretation's uniqueness claim, and leaves the two vote handlers' description intact; the old revision stays available; affected_uses empty because the validator only accepts objects recorded as uses of that revision), and as a new investigation with a Behavior stating the actual distribution. Two parts of the first finding survive and are now precisely scoped: only timeoutNow sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer, which is what makes the induced RequestVote winnable despite a known leader, and TimeoutNowRequest carries no term, so an expired transfer request from a sender that has lost leadership cannot be detected — a case needing no non-member at all. Counterevidence is kept prominent, including the bootstrap carve-out (an empty configuration list grants) and the fact that under the standard transport-trust assumption a member could obtain comparable effects with a higher-term AppendEntries. The second finding and the snapshot-cycle finding do not depend on uniqueness of the omission and are unaffected.
